chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: First money playing outside bars and in the District
summary: The boys made two dollars each outside bars, then seven in the District, and his mother was not angry.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: We made like two dollars a piece. Men was makin' like ten dollars a week and raising their family!
So then we're in business. You dig? Next week's... Now, I know what Ervin(?) Butler ain't givin' us. We got about maybe, say, three-fifths of what we made. He kept that other.

Next week... Next week he takes us in the District. We just go. And the police come and say "Take them kids out of here. They ain't got no business in here." But we was coinin'(?) (?). Boy, we must have made about seven dollars a piece. I didn't get home until about, like, around 11

o'clock, and when I hit the door, my mother said, "Boy, where you been?" I said, "Well, I went and made some money." She said, "You made some money?" [LAUGHS] I just thought I was gonna get smacked upside the head. And she said, "You made some money? Where could you go and do that?" I said, "Well, we was playing for them people, playing for them rich White people." "Them rich White people?" I put that "rich White people" to let her know I was around a nice place! [LAUGHING HELPLESSLY] Then I went inside to count that money. I gave her $4, and I kept one I'd stashed before, and it left me with $3. She wasn't mad.
Boy, the next day she told the whole family. Shit, I made more money than my uncles who was playing in the bands! She only gave me three dollars!
